_comment: Gopich-Szabo photon-by-photon kinetics. AutoForm over BurstGsViewModel. Left: where the photons come from and what scheme to fit. Right: the report, the fitted parameters, the transition-time scan and the states on the efficiency axis. Fit lives in the host toolbar; long help sits behind the ? button.

sections.label: TTTR folder
sections.description: Folder the raw TTTR files named in the burst table resolve against. Left empty, the burst table's own folder is used.

sections.label: Container
sections.description: TTTR container type of the raw files, or Auto to detect it.

sections.label: Donor channels
sections.description: Routing channels counted as donor photons, comma separated. This is colour 0.

sections.label: Acceptor channels
sections.description: Routing channels counted as acceptor photons, comma separated. This is colour 1. Photons in neither list — acceptor-excitation photons, for instance — are dropped.

sections.label: Macro-time tick [ns]
sections.description: Seconds per macro-time tick, in nanoseconds. Zero reads it from the file header. Every fitted rate is proportional to this, so a wrong value rescales the whole answer silently.

sections.label: Min photons/burst
sections.description: Bursts with fewer photons are dropped. A burst too short to show a spread of interphoton gaps contributes nothing to the kinetics and only costs time.

sections.label: Max bursts
sections.description: Keep at most this many bursts; 0 uses all of them. Lower it for a quick first look.

sections.title: Simulate instead
sections.description: Generate photons from a known two-state molecule. The honest way to learn what this method can resolve on your photon budget — and the only way to know the right answer.

sections.label: Simulate
sections.description: Fit simulated photons instead of the loaded files.

sections.label: k(1→2) [1/s]
sections.description: True forward rate of the simulated molecule.

sections.label: k(2→1) [1/s]
sections.description: True backward rate.

sections.label: E state 1
sections.description: True FRET efficiency of state 1.

sections.label: E state 2
sections.description: True FRET efficiency of state 2. States closer together than the shot noise cannot be separated however many photons you collect.

sections.label: Photon rate [kHz]
sections.description: Detected photons per second within a burst. This sets the fastest exchange that can be resolved at all: nothing faster than the interphoton time is visible.

sections.label: Bursts
sections.description: Number of simulated bursts.

sections.label: Photons/burst
sections.description: Photons in each simulated burst.

sections.label: Seed
sections.description: Random seed, so a simulation can be reproduced.

sections.label: States
sections.description: Number of kinetic states. Add one only when the BIC clearly falls: every extra state costs n more rates and always fits a little better.

sections.label: Initial rate [1/s]
sections.description: Starting value for every rate. Rates are optimised in log space, so this only needs to be the right order of magnitude.

sections.label: Fix efficiencies
sections.description: Hold the per-state efficiencies at their starting values and fit only the rates. Worth doing when the efficiencies are known from a static measurement: rates and efficiencies are the most strongly correlated pair in this problem.

sections.label: Optimiser
sections.description: Nelder-Mead is derivative-free and robust; L-BFGS-B is faster but leans on finite differences of a likelihood that is only piecewise smooth.

sections.label: Max iterations
sections.description: Optimiser iteration cap.

sections.label: Scan transition time
sections.description: After fitting, insert an explicit intermediate the molecule must cross and scan how long it takes. Two states only. Usually this returns an upper bound rather than a measurement, which is itself the useful answer.

sections.label: Scan points
sections.description: Points in the transition-time scan, spread logarithmically from 1 µs to 1 ms.

sections.label: Decode state path
sections.description: Compute the most likely state of every photon (Viterbi). An illustration of the fitted model, not a measurement: it draws a definite path even where the photons support none.

sections.label: Cross-check with H2MM
sections.description: Fit the same photons with the discrete-time H2MM engine and compare. The two share no code and parameterise time differently, so agreement is real evidence — and disagreement is worth chasing before you believe either.

columns.label: 1/k [µs]
columns.description: Mean waiting time for that transition — usually the more intuitive number.

columns.label: Population
columns.description: Equilibrium fraction implied by the fitted rates.

sections.title: State populations
sections.description: Where the fitted states sit on the efficiency axis and how much of the population each holds. Two states closer together than the shot-noise width of a burst cannot be separated no matter how the fit converges, so check this against the burst-wise E histogram before believing a narrow pair.

sections.title: Transition time
sections.description: How much the data prefer a transition of finite duration over an instantaneous one. The grey line is the instantaneous model. A curve that stays at zero for short durations and falls for long ones is the normal result: it sets an upper bound on the crossing time. Only a clear positive peak is a measurement, and it needs a likelihood-ratio test before it is one.
